t: The largest empire in history, ruling roughly a quarter of the world's people at its peak around 1920.
Naval supremacy, industrial power and the City of London spread its laws, parliaments and language worldwide.
Two world wars drained its wealth; after Indian independence in 1947 it dissolved within a few decades.
dyk: The Indian Civil Service ran a country of some 300 million people with a cadre of only about 1,000 to 1,200 senior officers.
ev: English settlers found Jamestown, Virginia, the first permanent colony in the Americas
Acts of Union join England and Scotland as the Kingdom of Great Britain
Treaty of Paris ends the Seven Years' War, stripping France of Canada
The Royal Navy wins at Trafalgar, securing a century of naval supremacy
The Indian Rebellion leads to the abolition of East India Company rule
India gains independence, removing the empire's most vital possession
The Suez Crisis exposes Britain's inability to act against US wishes
Britain hands Hong Kong to China, formally closing the imperial era
